name: Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol (inhaler)
className: Inhaled corticosteroid with long-acting beta2 agonist (ICS/LABA)

formulations.label: Inhalation powder (dry powder inhaler) 50/250
formulations.strengths: salmeterol 50 micrograms + fluticasone propionate 250 micrograms per dose (same SmPC also covers 50/100 and 50/500)
formulations.note: The COPD dose is 50/500 twice daily (the 50/250 strength is not the COPD dose); in children 4-11 years only the 50/100 strength is licensed.

src.q: This corresponds to a pre-dispensed dose of 50 micrograms of salmeterol (as salmeterol xinafoate) and 100, 250 or 500 micrograms fluticasone propionate.
Seretide (50 micrograms salmeterol and 500 micrograms fluticasone propionate) is indicated for the symptomatic treatment of patients with COPD

brandPrescribing.t: SPS: prescribing by brand is necessary when devices have different instructions for use and need patient training; dry powder inhalers are named as an example. Generic prescribing of inhalers can lead to an unfamiliar device, which could affect use and adherence.

src.q: When administration devices have different instructions for use and patients require training to use them.
adrenaline auto-injectors, dry powder inhalers
Generic prescribing of inhalers can lead to people being given an unfamiliar device which could affect usage and adherence.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Asthma: regular treatment where an ICS/LABA combination is appropriate (not controlled on ICS plus as-needed SABA, or already controlled on ICS and LABA). The 50/100 strength is not appropriate for severe asthma.

src.q: Seretide is indicated in the regular treatment of asthma where use of a combination product (long- acting β2 agonist and inhaled corticosteroid) is appropriate
Note: Seretide 50 microgram /100 microgram strength is not appropriate in adults and children with severe asthma.

items.t: COPD: FEV1 <60% predicted (pre-bronchodilator) with repeated exacerbations and significant symptoms despite regular bronchodilators. The COPD dose is 50/500 twice daily, so the clinic 50/250 strength is not the COPD dose.

src.q: Seretide (50 micrograms salmeterol and 500 micrograms fluticasone propionate) is indicated for the symptomatic treatment of patients with COPD, with a FEV1 <60% predicted normal (pre-bronchodilator) and a history of repeated exacerbations
One inhalation of 50 micrograms salmeterol and 500 micrograms fluticasone propionate twice daily.

items.t: Not intended for the initial management of mild asthma; inhaled corticosteroids remain first line for most patients.

src.q: Seretide is not intended for the initial management of mild asthma.
In general inhaled corticosteroids remain the first line treatment for most patients.

items.t: MHRA (asthma): always prescribe a LABA with an inhaled corticosteroid, and only when ICS alone does not control symptoms; do not start a LABA in rapidly deteriorating asthma; review regularly, lowest effective dose, stop if no benefit. (This product already contains an ICS.)

src.q: always prescribe LABA with concomitant ICS and only when ICS alone are not sufficient to control asthma symptoms
LABA should not be initiated in patients with rapidly deteriorating asthma
review LABA therapy regularly, prescribe the lowest effective dose, and stop if there is no benefit

items.t: Device and brand (SPS): prescribe by brand when devices differ in use and need training; dry powder inhalers are an example.

src.q: When administration devices have different instructions for use and patients require training to use them.
adrenaline auto-injectors, dry powder inhalers

items.t: NICE (asthma): if possible, use the same type of device for preventer and reliever when more than one inhaler is needed.

src.q: If possible, prescribe the same type of device to deliver preventer and reliever treatments where more than one inhaler is needed.

items.t: Asthma, adults and adolescents 12 years and over: one inhalation twice daily of 50/100, 50/250 or 50/500 (strength by severity). Titrate to the lowest dose that keeps control; once daily may be tried if adequate.

src.q: One inhalation of 50 micrograms salmeterol and 250 micrograms fluticasone propionate twice daily.
As an alternative, patients requiring a long-acting β2 agonist could be titrated to Seretide given once daily if, in the opinion of the prescriber, it would be adequate to maintain disease control.

items.t: COPD, adults: one inhalation of 50/500 twice daily.

src.q: One inhalation of 50 micrograms salmeterol and 500 micrograms fluticasone propionate twice daily.

items.t: Elderly and renal impairment: no dose adjustment. No data in hepatic impairment.

src.q: There is no need to adjust the dose in elderly patients or in those with renal impairment.
There are no data available for use of Seretide in patients with hepatic impairment.

items.t: Children 4 years and over: one inhalation of 50/100 twice daily only (maximum licensed fluticasone propionate 100 micrograms twice daily). The 50/250 strength is for 12 years and over. No data under 4 years.

src.q: Children 4 years and older: - One inhalation of 50 micrograms salmeterol and 100 micrograms fluticasone propionate twice daily.
The maximum licensed dose of fluticasone propionate delivered by Seretide Accuhaler in children is 100 microgram twice daily.
There are no data available for use of Seretide in children aged under 4 years.

items.t: Children and adolescents under 16 on high fluticasone doses (typically 1000 micrograms/day or more) are at particular risk of systemic effects; monitor height on prolonged treatment.

src.q: Children and adolescents <16 years taking high doses of fluticasone propionate (typically ≥ 1000 micrograms/day) may be at particular risk.
It is recommended that the height of children receiving prolonged treatment with inhaled corticosteroid is regularly monitored.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to fluticasone propionate, salmeterol or the excipient (lactose, which contains milk proteins).

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
Excipient: Lactose monohydrate (which contains milk proteins).

items.t: Not for acute symptoms (use a fast-acting reliever); do not start during an exacerbation or acutely deteriorating asthma; do not stop abruptly in asthma (down-titrate under supervision).

src.q: Seretide Accuhaler should not be used to treat acute asthma symptoms for which a fast- and short- acting bronchodilator is required.
Treatment with Seretide should not be stopped abruptly in patients with asthma due to risk of exacerbation.

items.t: Use with caution in severe cardiovascular disorders or heart rhythm abnormalities, diabetes, thyrotoxicosis, uncorrected hypokalaemia or predisposition to low potassium.

src.q: Seretide should be used with caution in patients with severe cardiovascular disorders or heart rhythm abnormalities and in patients with diabetes mellitus, thyrotoxicosis, uncorrected hypokalaemia or patients predisposed to low levels of serum potassium.

items.t: Adrenal suppression and acute adrenal crisis with prolonged high doses (rarely at 500 to under 1000 micrograms fluticasone); consider extra systemic steroid cover in stress or elective surgery.

src.q: Prolonged treatment of patients with high doses of inhaled corticosteroids may result in adrenal suppression and acute adrenal crisis.
Additional systemic corticosteroid cover should be considered during periods of stress or elective surgery.

items.t: Caution in active or quiescent pulmonary tuberculosis and fungal, viral or other airway infections.

src.q: Seretide should be administered with caution in patients with active or quiescent pulmonary tuberculosis and fungal, viral or other infections of the airway.

items.t: COPD: increased pneumonia incidence with inhaled corticosteroids; stay vigilant.

src.q: An increase in the incidence of pneumonia, including pneumonia requiring hospitalisation, has been observed in patients with COPD receiving inhaled corticosteroids.

items.t: Refer to an ophthalmologist if blurred vision or other visual disturbance.

src.q: If a patient presents with symptoms such as blurred vision or other visual disturbances, the patient should be considered for referral to an ophthalmologist

items.t: Beta-blockers (selective and non-selective): avoid unless there are compelling reasons.

src.q: Both non-selective and selective β blockers should be avoided unless there are compelling reasons for their use.

items.t: CYP3A inhibitors: ritonavir, ketoconazole, itraconazole, cobicistat (potent) and erythromycin (moderate) raise fluticasone exposure (Cushing's syndrome, adrenal suppression reported); ketoconazole raises salmeterol exposure (QTc, palpitations). Avoid unless benefit outweighs risk; if used, monitor for systemic corticosteroid effects.

src.q: Co-treatment with other potent CYP3A inhibitors, such as itraconazole and cobicistat-containing products, and moderate CYP3A inhibitors, such as erythromycin, is also expected to increase the systemic fluticasone propionate exposure

Combinations should be avoided unless the benefit outweighs the potential increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side-effects, in which case patients should be monitored for systemic corticosteroid side-effects.
The concomitant administration of ketoconazole should be avoided, unless the benefits outweigh the potentially increased risk of systemic side effects of salmeterol treatment.

items.t: Xanthines, steroids and diuretics may potentiate hypokalaemia: particular caution in acute severe asthma.

src.q: Particular caution is advised in acute severe asthma as this effect may be potentiated by concomitant treatment with xanthine derivatives, steroids and diuretics.

items.t: No dose adjustment in renal impairment.

src.q: There is no need to adjust the dose in elderly patients or in those with renal impairment.

items.t: No data in hepatic impairment; no dose advice stated.

src.q: There are no data available for use of Seretide in patients with hepatic impairment.

items.t: SmPC: over 1000 pregnancy outcomes show no malformative or feto/neonatal toxicity. Consider only if benefit to the mother outweighs any risk to the fetus; use the lowest effective fluticasone dose.

src.q: A large amount of data on pregnant women (more than 1000 pregnancy outcomes) indicates no malformative or feto/neonatal toxicity related to Seretide.
Administration of Seretide to pregnant women should only be considered if the expected benefit to the mother is greater than any possible risk to the fetus.

items.t: BUMPS: inhaled corticosteroids should be continued in pregnancy; no evidence they harm the baby.

src.q: Inhaled corticosteroids should be continued throughout pregnancy to ensure that breathing problems do not occur.
There is no evidence that use of inhaled corticosteroids in pregnancy harms the baby.

items.t: SmPC: unknown whether excreted in human milk; risk to the infant cannot be excluded. Decide whether to stop breastfeeding or stop therapy.

src.q: A risk to breastfed newborns/infants cannot be excluded. A decision must be made whether to discontinue breastfeeding or to discontinue Seretide therapy

items.t: SPS: inhaled fluticasone can be used during breastfeeding (salmeterol not covered on this page).

src.q: When applied to the skin, inhaled or used intranasally, fluticasone can be used during breastfeeding.

items.t: No human fertility data; animal studies showed no effect on fertility.

src.q: There are no data in humans. However, animal studies showed no effects of salmeterol or fluticasone propionate on fertility.

items.t: Very common: headache, nasopharyngitis (both also common or very common with placebo). Common: mouth and throat candidiasis, pneumonia and bronchitis (COPD), hypokalaemia, throat irritation, hoarseness/dysphonia, sinusitis, bruising, muscle cramps, fractures, joint and muscle pain. Tremor, palpitations and headache tend to be transient.

items.t: Paradoxical bronchospasm: treat straight away with a rapid-acting bronchodilator; stop this inhaler and assess.

src.q: Paradoxical bronchospasm responds to a rapid-acting bronchodilator and should be treated straightaway. Seretide Accuhaler should be discontinued immediately, the patient assessed and alternative therapy instituted if necessary.

items.t: Rare: anaphylactic reactions including shock, angioedema, bronchospasm; cardiac arrhythmias.

src.q: Anaphylactic reactions including anaphylactic shock
Rarely, Seretide may cause cardiac arrhythmias e.g. supraventricular tachycardia, extrasystoles and atrial fibrillation

items.t: Sudden, progressive loss of asthma control is potentially life-threatening: urgent medical assessment.

src.q: Sudden and progressive deterioration in control of asthma is potentially life-threatening and the patient should undergo urgent medical assessment.

items.t: Regular review so the strength stays optimal; reduce to the lowest effective dose.

src.q: Patients should be regularly reassessed by a doctor, so that the strength of Seretide they are receiving remains optimal and is only changed on medical advice.

items.t: Regularly monitor adrenocortical function after transfer from oral steroids; monitor height in children on prolonged treatment.

src.q: Therefore these patients should be treated with special care and adrenocortical function regularly monitored.
It is recommended that the height of children receiving prolonged treatment with inhaled corticosteroid is regularly monitored.

items.t: Stop at once if paradoxical bronchospasm occurs.

src.q: Seretide Accuhaler should be discontinued immediately, the patient assessed and alternative therapy instituted if necessary.

items.t: Open and prime by sliding the lever, close lips round the mouthpiece, inhale, then close the device. Rinsing the mouth or brushing teeth after use can reduce hoarseness and thrush.

src.q: The device is opened and primed by sliding the lever. The mouthpiece is then placed in the mouth and the lips closed round it. The dose can then be inhaled and the device closed.
may be relieved by rinsing the mouth with water and/or brushing the teeth after using the product

items.t: Use every day, even when well. Keep a reliever inhaler for acute attacks available at all times.

src.q: Patients should be made aware that Seretide Accuhaler must be used daily for optimum benefit, even when asymptomatic.
Patients should be advised to have their inhaler to be used for relief in an acute asthma attack available at all times.

items.t: See a doctor if more reliever is needed, the reliever works less well, or symptoms worsen after starting.

src.q: Increased requirements for use of reliever medication (short-acting bronchodilators), or decreased response to reliever medication indicate deterioration of control and patients should be reviewed by a physician.
